title: Assignment operators, precedence and parentheses

stages.name: Step 1: 6 / 2
stages.detail: / * % come before + -. Working left to right, 6 / 2 = 3. Expression: 10 + 3 * 3 - 4 % 3

stages.name: Step 2: 3 * 3
stages.detail: Next * (same level as /, left to right) gives 9. Expression: 10 + 9 - 4 % 3

stages.name: Step 3: 4 % 3
stages.detail: % is also at the high level, so it is done before + and -. 4 % 3 = 1. Expression: 10 + 9 - 1

stages.name: Step 4: 10 + 9
stages.detail: Now + and - (same level, left to right). 10 + 9 = 19. Expression: 19 - 1

stages.name: Step 5: 19 - 1
stages.detail: The last step gives the final answer: 18

visuals.title: Match the operator to its priority

pairs.meaning: Next: act on a single value
Then multiply, divide, remainder (left to right)
Then add and subtract (left to right)

goal: After this you can use = += -= *= /= %= and work out, step by step, the value of any expression with several operators.
warmup: In maths class you learned that 2 + 3 x 4 is 14, not 20, because multiplication goes before addition. A canteen bill works the same way: 2 teas at Rs. 40 each plus 1 sandwich at Rs. 150 is 2 * 40 + 150 = 230. Nobody adds 2 + 40 first. C++ follows the same order rules, and you can use brackets to change them.
definition: An assignment operator stores a value in a variable. The simple form is =. The compound forms (+= -= *= /= %=) change a variable using its own old value: x += 5 means x = x + 5. Precedence is the priority of operators: the higher one is done first. Associativity says which direction to go when operators have the same priority (usually left to right).
howItWorks: Step through the trace. For every expression C++ looks for brackets first, then * / %, then + -, and works from left to right inside each level. Assignment is always the last operation: the whole right side is calculated first, then the answer is stored in the variable.
syntax:
x = 10;          // store 10 in x
x += 5;          // x = x + 5
x -= 5;          // x = x - 5
x *= 5;          // x = x * 5
x /= 5;          // x = x / 5
x %= 5;          // x = x % 5

x *= y + 2;      // means x = x * (y + 2), NOT (x * y) + 2

// Priority, highest first:
// ( )  then  ++ -- unary-  then  * / %  then  + -  then  = += -= ...
a = b = c = 4;   // = goes right to left

explanation.text: The right side is worked out completely first: y * 2 = 6. Then x = x + 6 = 16.
The right side y + 3 = 5 is worked out first. Then x = 16 % 5 = 1.

steps.note: Right side first: y * 2 = 6. Then x = 10 + 6 = 16.
Right side first: y + 3 = 5. Then x = 16 % 5 = 1.

variations.when: Force an operation to happen first
For * / % and + -, equal priority runs left to right

mistakes.error: expected primary-expression before '=' token (no space allowed between + and =)
lvalue required as left operand of assignment (the left side of = must be a variable)

mistakes.wrong: int avg = a + b / 2;   // wants the average of a and b
mistakes.error: No error, but / is done before +, so only b is halved. Use brackets.
No error! It means x = (+5), so x becomes 5 and the old value is lost.

examTips: Order to remember: brackets, then * / %, then + -, then assignment last.
For equal priority, go left to right (but = and compound assignments go right to left).
Rewrite x op= expr as x = x op (expr), with brackets around the whole right side.
When unsure, add brackets. Extra brackets never hurt and often make your answer easier to mark.
In an exam, rewrite the expression after every step, like 10 + 3 * 3 - 4 % 3, so the marker can follow.
romanSummary: x += 5 ka matlab x = x + 5. Isi tarah -=, *=, /= aur %= hain.
Precedence ka matlab priority: pehle brackets ( ), phir * / %, phir + -, aur assignment sab se aakhir mein.
Same priority wale operators left se right chalte hain, jaise 100 / 10 / 2 = 5.
Assignment (=) right se left chalta hai, isliye a = b = c = 4 mein pehle c ko 4 milta hai.
Shak ho to brackets laga do, answer saaf aur sahi rehta hai.
